name: showreel-32-waiting

voice.text: Why does waiting feel shorter? One: the send button shrinks into a spinner. Two: the photo fades in, it never pops. Three: the toast eases in, then settles. Save these three for your next app.

experiment.change: slow-mo details compilation, try 3 (waiting), with size-matched element sound

caption:
Why does waiting feel shorter in some apps? ⏳ Three small motions that keep you company while the app works, each played at real speed, then slowed down.

1) The send button shrinks into a spinner: a transition on width with cubic-bezier(.65, 0, .35, 1), 500 ms.
2) The photo fades in, it never pops: opacity, and scale from 1.06 to 1, with cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .3, 1), 500 ms.
3) The toast eases in, then settles: @starting-style sets where it starts, and cubic-bezier(.2, .9, .3, 1.25) overshoots a little.

@starting-style works in Chrome 117, Firefox 129 and Safari 17.5; scale in Chrome 104, Firefox 72 and Safari 14.1.
Save it for your next app, or send it to a designer friend.

tip.title: Three motions that make waiting feel shorter
tip.why: A button that turns into a spinner, a photo that fades in and a toast that settles all say "working on it" without words, so the wait feels shorter than a frozen screen.
